profile.legal_name: Merck & Co., Inc. (MSD outside the US and Canada)
profile.founders_or_origin: Started as the US affiliate of Germany's Merck family firm (George Merck, Theodore Weicker); independent of Merck KGaA since 1917

top_products.name: Bridion
top_products.what: Reversal of neuromuscular blockade after surgery

venture_arm.name: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (Merck GHI Fund)

profile.summary: US drug and vaccine major whose sales are dominated by Keytruda, the world's top-selling medicine, with a large animal-health arm inherited from Schering-Plough's purchase of Organon BioSciences/Intervet. The 2009 Schering-Plough reverse merger shaped today's company; it later sold consumer care to Bayer and spun off Organon, and has since bought Acceleron, Prometheus, Verona, Cidara and Terns to diversify ahead of Keytruda's patent expiry.

events.description: Set up as the American arm of Germany's Merck; it was seized in WWI and became fully independent in 1917.
Schering Corporation, the former US unit of Schering AG, merges with Memphis consumer-products maker Plough to form Schering-Plough.
Merck forms a US joint venture with Sweden's Astra to market Astra drugs, the base of the later Astra Merck business.
Merck buys pharmacy-benefit manager Medco, renamed Merck-Medco, in a bet on vertical integration.
Merck's animal-health unit and Rhône-Mérieux combine into 50/50 animal-health joint venture Merial; Sanofi later buys Merck's half.
DuPont buys out Merck's half of the DuPont Merck Pharmaceutical joint venture.
Merck spins Merck-Medco off to shareholders as independent Medco Health Solutions, later bought by Express Scripts.
Schering-Plough buys Akzo Nobel's Organon human-health and Intervet animal-health units, bringing women's health and an animal-health franchise.
Merck combines with Schering-Plough in a reverse merger; the combined company takes the Merck name.
Merck and Sanofi drop their plan to merge Merial with Intervet/Schering-Plough into a combined animal-health venture.

events.result: Merck Animal Health / MSD Animal Health
events.description: The Intervet/Schering-Plough animal-health division is renamed Merck Animal Health (MSD Animal Health abroad).
Before Merck bought it, Cubist acquired Optimer (C. difficile drug Dificid) and Trius to expand its antibiotics line.
Merck sells its consumer-care business (Claritin, Coppertone, Dr. Scholl's) to Bayer.
Purchase of hepatitis C nucleotide developer Idenix to bolster Merck's HCV pipeline.
Merck buys hospital-antibiotics specialist Cubist (Cubicin, Zerbaxa).
Animal-health deal for livestock identification and monitoring company Antelliq (about $3.7B including debt).
Merck acquires HIF-2α inhibitor developer Peloton, source of kidney-cancer drug Welireg.
Adds ArQule's reversible BTK inhibitor nemtabrutinib for B-cell cancers.
Merck buys $1B of Seattle Genetics stock alongside an antibody-drug conjugate co-development deal.
Purchase of VelosBio and its ROR1-directed antibody-drug conjugate for blood cancers.
Merck buys autoimmune-disease biotech Pandion, a Roche Venture Fund-backed company.
Women's health, biosimilars and legacy brands are spun off as NYSE-listed Organon & Co. in June.
Acceleron purchase secures sotatercept, now Winrevair for pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Merck pays $200 per share for Prometheus and its TL1A antibody for inflammatory bowel disease.
Deal worth up to $3B for retinal-disease developer EyeBio and its Wnt-pathway antibody.
Purchase of preclinical brain-tumor drug developer Modifi Biosciences.
Merck buys Verona at $107 per ADS, adding COPD maintenance inhaler Ohtuvayre.
Acquisition of Cidara and its long-acting influenza preventive antiviral candidate closes in early 2026.
Merck buys Terns for its oral allosteric BCR-ABL1 inhibitor for chronic myeloid leukemia.
Merck Animal Health buys TARGAN, adding high-speed poultry biodevice technology.
Five years after the spin-off, Organon & Co. is acquired by India's Sun Pharma.
